t: That the Federal Building at 100 State Street, Rochester, New York, shall hereafter be known and designated as the “Kenneth B. Keating Federal Building”. Any reference in any law, map, regulation, document, record, or other paper of the United States to such building shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Kenneth B. Keating Federal Building”.

fable.w: This section only names a federal building and says existing references to it are deemed to use the new name. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but here it appears only in a list of documents that might mention the building and gives no agency authority to issue rules. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision.
fable.s: Any reference in any law, map, regulation, document, record, or other paper of the United States to such building shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Kenneth B. Keating Federal Building”.

qwen_block.w: This section simply designates the name of a federal building. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or comment periods mentioned.
qwen_block.s: That the Federal Building at 100 State Street, Rochester, New York, shall hereafter be known and designated as the “Kenneth B. Keating Federal Building”.

opus.w: This section only renames a federal building and says that existing references to it will be read as references to the new name. The word "regulation" sits in a list of documents ("law, map, regulation, document, record"), so it does not grant rulemaking authority or create any process involving outside parties. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue.
opus.b: **Step 1: Analysis.** The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking authority, which would count as participation under Example 6. That reading fails. The word "regulation" only appears in a list of existing documents whose references to the building will be read as references to the new name. The section gives no power to issue regulations, and it does not involve anyone outside the federal government in any decision. It simply names a building.
